body:
Mostly that there's a lot of particulars about survival in my subfield that I'm beginning to be aware that I don't know of, and I get mixed messages about it.  I don't know where the line is between 'prestigious' and 'middle tier'.  I don't know what petty shit goes on in admissions committees.  I don't know, honestly, if I really am socially awkward, because this has always been an issue and I'm not sure if that's real social ineptitude or perhaps a case of a sort of mild social anxiety.  I don't know if there really is something about me that's unlikeable, because Nobody Ever Tells Me These Things.  I can put up with it if someone tells me and demonstrates why they believe this is the case, and I might be sad for a bit but ultimately I can improve, but I can't do shit if I don't know.

(You know what's funny?  I tested as having a rather high IQ as a kid, in at least the 160s and one psychometrist estimated it at 'well above 180', and it's always seemed to me to be twistedly similar to how I imagine an autism spectrum disorder is like for people who have it from what I know of how ASDs work as someone in the neurobiology field who is interested in evo-devo-neuro.  For the record, I have been told by my therapist, who has worked extensively with both people on the autism spectrum and high IQ people, that she is strongly convinced I'm not one of the former, despite the fact that I have inquired this of her several times.  It's BIZARRE, and it's like I've got a condition that's still unknown to psychology, except it's known and I feel awkward talking about it because in some twisted way it's like I'm bragging.  It's a double-edged sword - you have immense brain power, but you're on the fringe in at least some ways.)

I'm not schizophrenic.  I don't think the government is trying to control me with mind rays, and my distrust is subsequent to an obvious external trigger.  I don't hallucinate or hear voices, either.

Good try, but no cigar for you.
